Summary:
Quick scoping for a 4-week security-focused pilot for Montclair Health: discuss success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, and security/compliance gating (SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS). AE + SE present. Customer security and infra leads attended.

Topics:
- Pilot goals & success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy)
- Workload sizing: p99 latency targets, expected qps, typical sequence lengths
- Benchmarks: token-throughput, cold-start, long-run stability, regression checks
- Timeline: pilot start, benchmark windows, review points
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 scope, ISO attestation, SSO/SAML, RBAC model, audit logs, KMS/HSM, VPC options

Transcript:
00:00 Laura Kim: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. We're here to scope the POC and specifically the security pilot requirements for Montclair Health. Aim to be efficient.
00:17 Jill Ramos (Redwood AE): Great, thanks Laura. Quick intros from our side, I'm Jill, AE, Samir is our SE, Hannah CSM, Eli solutions. We'll run through success criteria, then Samir will dive into sizing and benchmark approach.
00:34 Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick note: apologies if I mangle any names. We'll cover throughput, latency, and the security checklist - SOC two, ISO, SSO, RBAC and audit trails.
00:50 Daniel Ortiz (CISO): Good. From our side I care mostly about encryption at rest in K M S, audit logs retention, and SSO integration. We also need SOC 2 or equivalent evidence for the pilot.
01:08 Jill: Understood. High level pilot proposal: 4 weeks, first week onboarding + baseline, week two benchmark window, week three real workload run, week four wrap + review. Does that align with Montclair's timelines?
01:25 Maya Singh (PM): That works. We want to validate two things: 1) explicit latency/SLOs on 95/99 percentile, 2) correctness for clinical prompts - i.e., hallucination rate below our threshold.
01:38 Samir: For latency targets can you share p95/p99 numbers? Typical numbers we see on hosted are ~200ms p95 for short sequences but depends on model and quantization.
01:50 Chris Park (Infra): We're looking for p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms for typical 256-token sequences. QPS expected 12 sustained with 60 burst.
02:05 Samir: Good, that's helpful. For sizing we'll plan a dedicated benchmark rig: a small dedicated instance on Redwood Dedicated to mirror production plus a hosted variant for comparison. We'll run steady-state qps and peak bursts.
02:22 Laura: On security - we need SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 evidence. Also SSO with SAML v2, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with at least 3 roles, and audit logs with 12 month retention. Is that feasible?
02:42 Jill: Yes, we can share our SOC 2 report and ISO attestation. For SAML and SCIM we support SSO integrations - we'll propose a short setup during onboarding. Audit logs can be exported; retention may depend on add-on - we'll confirm.
03:00 Daniel: KMS - do you use customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed? Encryption at rest is a big ask.
03:09 Samir: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in Private and Dedicated options; in hosted we have Redwood-managed encryption by default but can do customer KMS in Private deployments. For the pilot we can run in a dedicated VPC with customer KMS if needed.
03:26 Maya: Good. Also need to confirm data handling: logs, prompts, and responses - for the pilot we require logs to be segregated and not used to train models.
03:36 Jill: We can commit to no-training clause for pilot data and provide contractual language. We'll send the data handling addendum.
03:44 Chris: What about audit logs? What fields are included and can we forward them to our SIEM?
03:52 Samir: Logs include request id, timestamp, user, route, model version, tokens in/out, and error codes. We can push to customer syslog or S3 in a secure channel - also support forwarding to Splunk/Datadog via connector.
04:08 Daniel: Are there RBAC primitives for least privilege? We want fine-grained control for dev vs prod vs compliance roles.
04:16 Eli Torres (Solutions Eng): Yes - roles can be scoped per project and per model route; you can limit create/deploy/fallback. We can demo RBAC in the console during onboarding.
04:28 Laura: On benchmarks: we need to run three tests - cold start latency, sustained throughput, and regression test against clinical prompt set. Can Redwood run the regression evaluation and provide per-prompt diff?
04:44 Samir: Yes, we can run eval harnesses and output per-prompt scores. We also recommend a baseline model and a quantized variant to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:56 Maya: For the regression metric, we'll give you a scoring rubric - tolerance on hallucinations per 100 responses.
05:05 Jill: Great. We'll add that to the success criteria doc. Success criteria suggested from Redwood side: p95/p99 latency within target, error rate < 0.5%, hallucination below your threshold, throughput sustain at 12 qps with acceptable tail latency, audit logs available and delivered to your SIEM, SSO + SCIM in place.
05:26 Daniel: Sounds reasonable. Regarding timeline - when can you start the pilot? We need infra windows.
05:33 Jill: We can start onboarding as early as 2026-11-29 pending NDA and network whitelists. Benchmarks ideally week of 2026-12-06. Does that align?
05:43 Chris: Yes week of 12/6 is fine. We'll need a maintenance window Monday morning for VPC peering.
05:52 Samir: Noted. On workload sizing: please provide sample payloads (typical prompt size, average response length). For planning, we assume average request 256 tokens in + 128 tokens out. If you can upload a representative sample we'll size the GPU pool accordingly.
06:08 Maya: We'll upload a 24-hour sample and some peak traces by 2026-11-28.
06:14 Samir: For benchmarks we'll run three model variants: base open model, quantized 4-bit, and a Redwood-verified low-latency variant. We'll capture token/sec, p50/p95/p99, and cost per 1k tokens.
06:29 Laura: On compliance docs, we need the actual SOC 2 whitepaper and ISO cert - can you send them?
06:35 Jill: We'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 attestation, and our product security overview. Also network diagram showing VPC peering options.
06:46 Daniel: For SSO, our IdP is Okta. Are there known issues?
06:51 Eli: Okta is fully supported for SAML & SCIM. We have setup guides and can do a quick config session.
07:02 Maya: One more: data residency. Some PHI must remain in-region. Can the dedicated cluster be provisioned in us-east-1 and ensure data stays there?
07:12 Samir: Yes for Dedicated and Private we can pin region. Hosted tier may not guarantee region-specific residency unless on an enterprise plan; we'll propose Dedicated for the pilot.
07:22 Laura: Let's talk about legal; procurement will need a DPA, BAA, and security addendum. Is Redwood ready to sign standard BAA for the pilot?
07:32 Jill: Yes, we can provide a BAA and DPA; legal review usually takes 1-2 weeks. We'll kick that off.
07:40 Daniel: What about long-term: if results are good we may want on-prem option. Do you support air-gapped installs?
07:48 Samir: We do offer Private deployments for on-prem or air-gapped in enterprise contracts. We'll include the options in the follow-up doc.
07:57 Chris: Any known limits around KV cache or session stickiness that could affect latency tests?
08:03 Samir: Our runtime uses KV cache and continuous batching; we can enable prefix caching to lower latency for repeated prompts. We'll note cache warm-up in the benchmark plan.
08:14 Maya: Can we get a cost projection for the pilot? Even rough per-hour GPU cost and an estimate of expected token costs?
08:22 Jill: We'll send a draft estimate after Samir sizes the cluster. It will include Dedicated reserved-hour costs and host vs dedicated deltas.
08:30 Daniel: Competitors - we may be evaluating Anthropic for safety features. Anything we should know?
08:36 Jill: We often benchmark against Anthropic/OpenAI. We'll include a comparative sheet if you'd like, but we'll focus on meeting your security needs.
08:46 Maya: On deliverables: we expect a pilot plan doc, SOC/ISO pack, benchmark plan, and a schedule for demo + final review.
08:54 Jill: We'll deliver those; include the action items and owners.
09:01 Laura: Ok let's do a quick recap and confirm next steps.
09:05 Jill: Recap: Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO, network diagram, pilot success criteria template, benchmark plan. Customer to provide sample payloads, SSO contacts, and compliance reviewers. Pilot target start week 2026-11-29 with benchmark window week of 2026-12-06.
09:25 Daniel: Agree. I'll confirm the compliance reviewers and get back by 11/30.
09:30 Maya: We'll upload sample payloads by 11/28.
09:34 Jill: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and an onboarding session for Okta SAML.
09:40 Laura: Thanks all. That was useful.
09:43 Jill: Thanks everyone, we'll email the deck and docs shortly.
09:48 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and dropped punctuation; some acronyms transcribed imperfectly (KMS sometimes appears as K M S).
